editorial_decision_gate.draft_heading: Key Contact Points and Questions to Review Under an Emergency Roof Title
editorial_decision_gate.proposed_text:
When making emergency contact during an active roof leak, addressing every key point and question under your service title helps ensure prompt preparation by emergency dispatch teams. Before placing the phone call, observe where water is entering the building, whether structural damage or missing shingles are visible from ground level, and if ceiling surfaces or electrical fixtures are directly threatened. Organizing these specific facts before calling allows the dispatch representative to document the critical details needed for safety recommendations.

Property owners should also summarize key situational details to discuss during the call. Record when water intrusion was first noticed, whether severe storm winds or fallen debris caused visible damage, and whether the building is a residential or commercial property. Having this practical information ready helps incoming personnel anticipate access requirements and select appropriate temporary tarping or mitigation equipment prior to arriving for an on-site evaluation.

Finally, ensure that work areas and entryway access points remain unobstructed while waiting for assistance. Keep interior pathways clear to attic hatches or upper levels, move vehicles away from exterior roof lines, and keep pets and family members safely distant from compromised structural areas. Once the crew arrives, completes their initial evaluation, and presents a cost estimate for review, you can grant approval for immediate leak mitigation.
